messages.content: BRCA1和BRCA2基因在智人和黑猩猩中編碼的蛋白質序列是什麼？

function.name: get_protein_sequence
function.description: Retrieve the protein sequence encoded by a human gene. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

species.description: The species for which the gene is to be analyzed.

message.reasoning:
The user asks: "BRCA1和BRCA2基因在智人和黑猩猩中編碼的蛋白質序列是什麼？" They want the protein sequences encoded by BRCA1 and BRCA2 genes in Homo sapiens (human) and Pan troglodytes (chimpanzee). We have a tool get_protein_sequence that can retrieve the protein sequence encoded by a human gene. It accepts gene name and species optional. So we need to call the tool twice for each gene? Actually we need sequences for both species. The tool can specify species. So we can call get_protein_sequence with gene=BRCA1, species=Homo sapiens; then gene=BRCA1, species=Pan troglodytes; similarly for BRCA2. But the tool only retrieves the protein sequence encoded by a human gene. It says species default is Homo sapiens. But we can specify species. So we can call it for chimp. That should work.

We need to provide the gene name. The gene names are "BRCA1" and "BRCA2". The species for chimp is "Pan troglodytes". So we will call the tool four times: get_protein_sequence for BRCA1 Homo sapiens, get_protein_sequence for BRCA1 Pan troglodytes, get_protein_sequence for BRCA2 Homo sapiens, get_protein_sequence for BRCA2 Pan troglodytes. Then we will return the results. The tool returns any. We need to parse the output. The tool likely returns the protein sequence string. We'll just return the sequences. The user wants the sequences. So we will call the tool for each gene/species pair.
